original_question: Does there exist a Borel invariant class C of closed subgroups of S∞ whose isomorphism relation is not Borel reducible to graph isomorphism?
target_in_paper: Problem 22 in Section 6 ("Complexity of isomorphism of oligomorphic groups"), specifically its first sentence. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
correct_elements: Your draft gets the core target essentially right: it asks for an existential example of a Borel, invariant class of closed subgroups of S∞ whose isomorphism relation is not Borel reducible to graph isomorphism, which is exactly the first sentence of Problem 22 up to minor wording. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
missing_details: The paper's exact wording is "a Borel, invariant class," so it is better to make explicit that these are two separate requirements on the class C, rather than the potentially ambiguous phrase "Borel invariant class." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

In the immediate surrounding context, the subsection is about complexity of isomorphism for topological groups, and Problem 19 explicitly speaks of topological isomorphism; so the intended reading here is topological isomorphism of closed subgroups of S∞, not merely abstract group isomorphism. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

Problem 22 does not stop with the first existence question: it immediately asks the sharper follow-up "Analytic complete?" Your draft omits this stronger companion question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

Problem 22 also asks for a specific test case: "How about the class of pro-countable groups?" Your draft does not mention this paper-specific specialization. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

There are no ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic-quantifier issues here; the hidden assumptions are instead descriptive-set-theoretic and topological, namely the Borel-class setting and the topological-isomorphism reading. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
refined_question: Does there exist a class C of closed subgroups of S∞ = Sym(ω) such that C is Borel and invariant under topological isomorphism, and the topological isomorphism relation on C is not Borel reducible to graph isomorphism? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 22, not a broader neighboring issue. Problem 22 asks, in exactly the direction of your draft, whether there is "a Borel, invariant class of closed subgroups of S∞ with isomorphism relation not Borel below graph isomorphism," and then adds two further paper-specific refinements: whether such a relation could be analytic complete, and whether this happens for pro-countable groups. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972)) The nearby context matters: the subsection is titled "Complexity of isomorphism of oligomorphic groups," Problem 19 asks about topological isomorphism, and Theorem 20 discusses topological automorphism groups and quotients, so the natural stand-alone sharpening is to state the question using topological isomorphism explicitly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972)) Because your draft already matches the first sentence of Problem 22 quite closely but leaves that topological reading implicit and omits the two follow-up clauses, it is strong but not fully complete as a paper-faithful stand-alone formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
